fulfillment_judgment.auxiliary_material: Section 5.2 and Table 3 summarize overall antibiotic impact on ICI efficacy across histologies (Routy, Derosa, Pinato, etc.), supporting the general negative association. Section 5.4 and Table 4 discuss timing windows (30 days before/after initiation) which may confound class-specific effects. Section 8 Discussion highlights the difficulty in extrapolating preclinical data and the presence of indication biases.
fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Use this review to cite the existence of class-comparison studies (Ahmed, Chalabi, Gaucher) and the prevailing view that 'broad-spectrum' activity (particularly against anaerobes) is the primary risk factor rather than a specific chemical class. Acknowledge the conflicting evidence in the review's discussion. For the planning gap, note that while ≥2 comparative studies are identified via this review, their discordant results mean the gap question (is there a significant difference/safe class?) remains partially unanswered, supporting the alternative success criterion path that existing material primarily supports a 'broad-spectrum' overall effect warning.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The supplied material identifies studies that compared antibiotic classes but reports conflicting conclusions (Ahmed et al. suggest narrow-spectrum is safer, while Chalabi et al. and Gaucher et al. found no significant class-specific differences). The specific head-to-head comparison between β-lactams and fluoroquinolones is not definitively resolved as they are often grouped under 'broad-spectrum' in the cited analyses. A consensus on which specific class is 'relatively safe' is not established.
fulfillment_judgment.useful_material: Section 5.5 'Importance of the Antibiotic Treatment Modality: Molecule and Spectrum' reports on studies comparing antibiotic classes: Ahmed et al. [78] found narrow Gram-positive spectrum antibiotics (vancomycin, daptomycin, linezolid) had no impact on response rate, whereas broad-spectrum antibiotics (β–lactams, quinolones, cyclines) affected response rate and PFS; Chalabi et al. [79] examined several antibiotic classes but found no significantly impairing class for ICI survival; Gaucher et al. [6] found no OS difference between amoxicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, and other antibiotics. Section 5.1 notes clindamycin (broad anaerobe activity) causes durable microbiota perturbations.
